newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Cycling-Tour de France opens with sprint around Dublin.
newsitem.headline: Cycling-Tour de France opens with sprint around Dublin.

text.p: The Tour de France will start with a sprint through the streets of Dublin next year before moving into the Irish countryside for two days, officials said on Thursday.
The Tour will be launched outside the European mainland for the first time when it starts with a seven-km timed prologue trial around Dublin on July 11.

The second day will provide riders with their first taste of climbing when they must pass through the Wicklow Hills along the east coast in a 175-km (110-mile) leg which finishes in Dublin's Phoenix Park.
On the third day, commemorating a main site of the 1798 rebellion against British rule of Ireland, riders will have an easier 200-km (125-mile) ride from Enniscorthy, County Wexford to Cork city.
The Irish government and Tour director general, Jean-Marie Leblanc, signed a race agreement in Dublin on Thursday.
The race will coincide with the 200th anniversary of a rebellion led by the Protestant Wolfe Tone who was inspired by the French revolution..
